purpose: Isocarboxazid is used to treat depression, especially when other antidepressants have not worked well. It can help improve your mood, energy, sleep, and overall sense of wellbeing. Doctors usually try other antidepressants first before prescribing this one.
how_it_works: Your brain uses certain natural chemicals called neurotransmitters — like serotonin, dopamine, and norepinephrine — to help regulate your mood. This medication works by blocking an enzyme called monoamine oxidase, which normally breaks down these chemicals. By blocking that enzyme, more of these mood-lifting chemicals stay active in your brain, which helps ease depression.
common_side_effects: Dizziness when standing up quickly, drowsiness, dry mouth, constipation, trouble sleeping, headache, nausea, blurred vision, and weight gain. You may also feel lightheaded or faint if you get up too fast from sitting or lying down.
warnings: This is a very important one: you must avoid certain foods containing tyramine while taking this medication — including aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented products, red wine, and beer. Eating these foods can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure. You also cannot take this medication with many other medications, including other antidepressants, cold medicines, or pain relievers like meperidine, as dangerous interactions can occur. Always check with your pharmacist before taking any new medication or supplement. Do not stop this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken by mouth twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time, up to a maximum of 60 mg per day divided into smaller doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing is adjusted individually.
